en.question: An agent must never run a destructive shell command such as rm -rf. The team adds a firm instruction to the system prompt. Why is this insufficient, and what is the right mechanism?

options.text: Prompts are probabilistic guidance; a hook can inspect and block the command.
The instruction is sufficient, because system prompts are obeyed strictly.
options.note: System prompts influence behaviour strongly but are not enforcement.

options.text: Lower the sampling temperature so destructive commands are never selected.
options.note: Temperature does not create a safety boundary of any kind.

options.text: Use a smaller model tier, which attempts fewer destructive operations.
options.note: Model size does not constrain what the harness will execute.

en.explanation: This is the deterministic-versus-probabilistic distinction the exam returns to repeatedly. A hook runs as code at a defined lifecycle point, inspects the pending action, and can deny it outright.
